newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says peso devaluation unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says peso devaluation unlikely.

text.p: The Philippine Central bank will not allow a devaluation of the peso, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said in a statement on Monday.
He issued this clarification after a Singapore-based newspaper misquoted him saying the peso may devalue against the U.S. dollar.
"The Philippine peso is based on market forces and not determined by the government," De Ocampo said.
"The Philippines will not resort to any shift in policy to a fixed rate system that saw a downfall of the financial system in Mexico two years ago and in Thailand just recently."
The Philippine Central Bank on Monday raised its overnight borrowing rate by six percentage points to 30 percent to defend the peso against speculation.
Just last week, the Central Bank implemented a nine percentage-point increase in its key rate to 24 percent after Thailand's de facto devaluation of the baht.
